listenerOrDispatch.text: A successful tick alone decrements the accumulator and advances the substep count. A failed or refused tick does not pretend that a simulation interval completed. AFTER_PHYSICS retains its original normal-return behavior, including a nonthrowing pause in BEFORE_PHYSICS; a thrown callback still propagates through the original error path. Pausing during collection, solver, writeback or dispatch is an early reentrant refusal, not a partial pause.

Native coefficient input and actual PhysicsMaterial identity are separate facts. Only a successful original Collider/System cache-and-listener operation may commit the corresponding actual asset identity to the private owner roster. A cloning getter must notify its real returned clone without reading Collider.material as an ownership-discovery shortcut.

The owner barrier opens before any before/candidate reader, clone allocation, listener operation or native delegate. Internal native delegation requires one private exact-operation authority, never a temporary unregistration or phase reset to idle. All affected owners are preflighted before effects. Observer tickets report delegate entry/return, cache writes and listener progress as JavaScript facts, not inferred native atomicity.

Native success followed by JS listener/cache/readback failure faults the affected owner and retains committed facts. Unknown native mutation stays unknown. Retain old, candidate and actually observed identity references separately for cleanup; do not claim rollback from a candidate value or restored coefficient alone. A failure with undefined, null or zero is still a real primary failure. Shared-asset propagation and protected subscription integrity remain a later explicit boundary, not implied by clone notification.

Required controls include disabled manual step refusal before native calls, manual autoSimulation mode with no queue clearing, BEFORE_PHYSICS pause with preserved backlog, caught reentrant pause with no cache change, failure between prepared commits, clone allocation/listener failures, same-object and equal-id distinct-material cases, shared ownership and native-success/JS-failure cleanup. No design document, pure observer test or Node HEADLESS run changes the 2,128 formal required cells from NOT_RUN.

During any active Box3D collection, final validation, command commit, or event-dispatch transaction, all calls to the original Node.addComponent in that Cocos realm reject at entry, before class-name resolution, user constructor properties, dependency recursion or constructor execution. This includes orphan and unrelated Nodes, UI/2D components, subclasses and user components. The compatibility restriction is deliberate and bounded to these transactions. It does not claim a physics-class-only filter. Outside such transactions, with no lease, original component construction behavior remains.

Import and exercise the actual engine entry points, not copied setter bodies. Verify unchanged cache/flags/arrays/material identity/listener bindings/accumulator and zero native or lifecycle callback effects at refusal. Include a protected later child, two owners sharing material, orphan/UI/2D component creation, constructor and requirement getter sentinels, and no-lease original behavior. Then qualify the actual World callback/validation/commit/release path against fresh schema-matched WASM. Until then no formal required cell is PASS.

explicitOnceOrRetirement.text: Do not temporarily release a target transform lease to make writeback succeed. Compose distinct owner-held exact grants for the transaction lease and every target lease covering the written Node; invoke the actual setter once at the innermost grant. All grants must refer to the same copied expected value and be consumed before listener callbacks. Preserve post-setter expected local TRS, world pose, ancestor basis, and final whole-batch verification. Foreign ownership remains a refusal.

Source controls, synthetic binding failures and finite Node WASM contracts must remain separately labeled; none change the 2128 formal cells from NOT_RUN.

explicitOnceOrRetirement.text: All accepted user submissions have a strictly increasing safe-integer sequence within the current world generation. Queue retention stores original accepted records; target reduction is a non-destructive view until commit/cancellation. Superseded target records can therefore still be counted as accepted-but-unconsumed entries. Gaps after cancelled/failed attempts are legal; sequence reuse/wrap is not. Ordinary impulses are consumed once, including catch-up ticks. `tickIndex` denotes the next completed logical tick and does not advance on refusal; `attemptId` is a separate diagnostic-only counter, never a simulation tick or command consumption identity.

Hooks and continuous handles share one stable registration order. At each candidate tick, snapshot the enabled roster and descriptor copies once. Pre-tick accepted commands precede producer contributions. Each continuous producer contributes force first, then torque, at its roster position; exact-zero components generate no command and do not wake a body. A nonzero force with an offset includes its induced torque; an explicit descriptor torque is a separate later operation. No producer runs during scene-sync-only calls or merely because a render frame elapsed.

It removes every accepted, unconsumed **user** entry for that body: force/torque/linear or angular impulse, teleport, target set/target clear, and ordinary clear-force/clear-velocity/clear-state. It does not remove internal scene synchronization, automatic target idle-zero, or lifecycle-required paired-zero obligations. Count one removed accepted record per original submission, including retained superseded target records; do not count vector axes, projected native calls, already retired entries or protected cleanup. Return zero when none exist.

Cancelling a target set/clear leaves the active target handle owned; with no explicit surviving intent, its next executable tick still clears paired velocity. Cancelling a teleport does not resurrect previously **retired** intent; because this operation removes all of this body's pending user entries, no older pending target is revived either. A later setTarget/teleport is a new sequence.

6. Protected dispose/revoke zero dominates ordinary user intent and cannot be overwritten by a later target. Once dispose is requested, new setTarget/clear/teleport for that body rejects until the protected cleanup settles and ownership is released. A later explicit teleport after release uses ordinary admission.
- `teleport R → target B`: R executes once, B plans from R's origin/COM/inertia. Target does not subsequently SetTransform to correct arrival.

Queued user records and all reduction decisions retire only after a known whole-batch commit or explicit cancellation. A pure rejected reset or later command cannot destructively cancel an earlier accepted target. No command is replayed after committed/unknown failure.
- Native status zero then copy/readback failure: committed; retire candidate, invalidate/fault, never replay or advance step to conceal the failure.

listenerOrDispatch.text: Create/update/enable are configuration operations outside a callback/step/event-dispatch transaction and require an unpaused ready world. Disable/dispose may also run while paused for cleanup, but not reentrantly during a transaction. Application teardown uses its internal cleanup path, not these admission restrictions to skip cleanup.

`cancelPendingBox3DCommands(body): number` is a pure queue operation allowed only in the **unpaused ready configuration phase**, not in a hook, step, event-dispatch transaction, faulted state or teardown. It validates the current initialized body/world/full-generation ownership, but does not require valid mass geometry, pose, or command arithmetic. A pending-invalid body or arithmetic-overflow queue must remain cancellable. Disabled/static bodies with still-valid ownership may return zero; stale/destroyed objects reject and their owning teardown already clears their entries.
